title: 18 - It’s Getting Worse
summary: [[character:riker]] stands outside the police lines at a run-down apartment building in a Brazilian favela, where an attack that tore away part of its ground floor has killed sixty-three people so far and left the structure fit only to be condemned. Brazil's [[character:benedito|Minister Benedito]], more frightened than angry, calls to complain that this is the third attack this month with no arrests; Riker, responsible only for the global emigration effort and present as a consultant, points him to Brazil's internal security forces and the [[organization:united-nations|UN]], lends [[technology:mining-drones]] to the rescuers and rings the site with surveillance drones against a follow-up attack. The attackers make no announcements or demands and seem simply to be targeting Brazil, of which Florianópolis is nearly all that remains. At a remote UN session, [[character:ambassador-gerrold|Gerrold]] of New Zealand again rails against Riker and the failure to stop the sabotage while Riker feigns attention through his public avatar and rolls his eyes in his [[technology:vr|VR]], until the Maldives' [[character:sharma|Minister Sharma]] rebukes him for repeating old speeches and asks him to take his problem with replicants offline, to the delegates' approval. The agenda turns to [[location:earth]]'s deteriorating climate: several higher-latitude enclaves are nearing non-viability, [[vessel:exodus-4]] and [[vessel:exodus-5]] are due to launch this month, the UN has confirmed that the island nations will go to [[location:eta-cassiopeiae-3]], and delegates disagree over whether to change the emigration order or move the troubled enclaves into vacated territory. Missing [[character:homer]], whose mockery of the meetings usually helps him through, Riker hands the video window to a sandbox Bob and slips away.
